citationText: 6. Most of this comes from Everson, op. cit., pp. 53 – 73 . Philo Farnsworth applied for his first patent for a television system in January 1927. See P. T. Farnsworth, U.S. Patent No. 1,773,980 filed Jan. 7, 1927; issued Aug. 26, 1930. “Television System.” Unknown to Philo Farnsworth, a similar patent had been applied for earlier in Germany. See Max Dieckmann and Rudolf Hell, German (DRP) No. 450,187. Filed Apr. 5, 1925: issued Oct. 3, 1927. However, this patent was not granted until after Farnsworth had applied for his patent in the U.S., so Farnsworth was quite unaware of its existence. While this certainly gives Dieckmann and Hell priority of invention, they could never get their device to operate.
